pr.body:
Refs STREAM-266

Compression helped a lot bring the time on the main thread down. We now think we can scale down the consumers. However, we also need to ensure the flusher can keep up. So let's make the flusher spawn a process per redis shard. 

We think this is easier to do than making the process_spans/insert_spans multiprocessed. Over time we can offload mroe things like statistics/metrics to the flusher, and keep the main thread minimal.
pr.title: ref(span-buffer): Introduce multiprocessed flusher

raw_findings.body: Processes created by the spawn context are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which subclasses BaseProcess directly and is NOT a subclass of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context class), so the isinstance check is False and kill() is never called. The old code called self.process.kill() unconditionally. Now _create_process_for_shards spawns a second process for the same shards while the hung one keeps running and its handle is overwritten in self.processes, leaking it; if the hung process later resumes, two flushers read the same Redis shard queues concurrently and produce duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Hung flusher processes are restarted without being killed, leaking processes and allowing duplicate concurrent flushing of the same shards.
raw_findings.impact: Processes created by the spawn context are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which subclasses BaseProcess directly and is NOT a subclass of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context class), so the isinstance check is False and kill() is never called. The old code called self.process.kill() unconditionally. Now _create_process_for_shards spawns a second process for the same shards while the hung one keeps running and its handle is overwritten in self.processes, leaking it; if the hung process later resumes, two flushers read the same Redis shard queues concurrently and produce duplicate segments to the buffered-segments topic.
raw_findings.root_cause: New type guard uses multiprocessing.Process, which does not match SpawnProcess instances created via the spawn context.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Check against the base class, e.g. `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` (or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`), so kill() is actually invoked on spawn-context processes before restarting.
raw_findings.title: Hung flusher process is never killed because SpawnProcess fails isinstance(multiprocessing.Process) check
raw_findings.trigger: A flusher process spawned via multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process hangs (is_alive() is True but healthy_since is stale beyond spans.buffer.flusher.max-unhealthy-seconds), causing _ensure_processes_alive to take the restart path with cause="hang".

raw_findings.body: The added wait does nothing; the comment claims it gives flusher threads time to process, but no time is actually granted. The test's correctness still depends entirely on step.join(), so the intended race mitigation for the multi-process flusher is absent and the test can remain flaky.
raw_findings.evidence:
# Give flusher threads time to process after drift change
    time.sleep(0.1)
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test synchronization code is dead, leaving the multi-process flush race unmitigated and the comment misleading.
raw_findings.impact: The added wait does nothing; the comment claims it gives flusher threads time to process, but no time is actually granted. The test's correctness still depends entirely on step.join(), so the intended race mitigation for the multi-process flusher is absent and the test can remain flaky.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new wait uses the module attribute time.sleep that the same test has already replaced with a no-op.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Call the real sleep (e.g. save `real_sleep = time.sleep` before monkeypatching, or use `from time import sleep` bound before patching as test_flusher.py does), or remove the misleading no-op call and comment.
raw_findings.title: Added synchronization sleep in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched in the same test
raw_findings.trigger: test_basic runs `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at the top of the test, so the later `time.sleep(0.1)` call resolves to the patched no-op lambda.

raw_findings.body: Unused method adds a second, untested restart entry point that can silently drift from the real restart logic and confuses readers about which restart path is authoritative.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Dead code accumulates in the flusher, degrading maintainability and inviting divergent duplicate logic.
raw_findings.impact: Unused method adds a second, untested restart entry point that can silently drift from the real restart logic and confuses readers about which restart path is authoritative.
raw_findings.root_cause: A helper method was added during the multiprocess refactor but never referenced.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Delete _create_process_for_shard, or wire it into the code path that actually needs per-shard restarts.
raw_findings.title: _create_process_for_shard is dead code with no call sites
raw_findings.trigger: Code review or maintenance of flusher.py: repository search shows no callers of _create_process_for_shard; all restart paths go through _create_process_for_shards directly.

raw_findings.body: The same dimension is exposed under two different tag keys across related metrics, breaking cross-metric grouping/filtering in dashboards and making the tag cardinality intent unclear.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Observability data for the flusher cannot be correlated across metrics by shard tag.
raw_findings.impact: The same dimension is exposed under two different tag keys across related metrics, breaking cross-metric grouping/filtering in dashboards and making the tag cardinality intent unclear.
raw_findings.root_cause: The per-process metric tagging added in this patch uses inconsistent tag key names for the same value.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a single tag key (e.g. "shards", since the value is a comma-joined list) for all three metric emissions in the flush loop.
raw_findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: 'shard' vs 'shards' for the same shard_tag value
raw_findings.trigger: Any flush cycle emits spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes tagged with key "shard" (R185, R195) but spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce tagged with key "shards", all carrying the same shard_tag value.

raw_findings.body: Operators and reviewers are misled about the process topology (one process per shard) when the default behavior is one shared process for all shards; capacity planning and debugging assumptions based on the docstring will be wrong.
raw_findings.evidence: Creates one process per shard for parallel processing.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale/incorrect documentation about the new concurrency model.
raw_findings.impact: Operators and reviewers are misled about the process topology (one process per shard) when the default behavior is one shared process for all shards; capacity planning and debugging assumptions based on the docstring will be wrong.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new class docstring describes only the uncapped case and ignores the max_processes limit introduced in the same patch.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: State that the flusher creates min(max_processes, num_shards) processes and distributes shards round-robin, noting the CLI default of 1 process.
raw_findings.title: Docstring claims one process per shard, contradicting max_processes capping and the CLI default of 1
raw_findings.trigger: Reading the SpanFlusher docstring while the constructor actually creates min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards)) processes, and the consumer CLI passes --flusher-processes with a default of 1, so the common deployment gets a single process handling all shards.

raw_findings.body: N identical cluster-wide memory INFO scans per submit (N = number of flusher processes), each buffer also holding its own duplicate parent-side Redis connection; used and available are each summed N times, adding redundant Redis load with no additional information.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Redundant Redis INFO traffic and duplicate connections scale with flusher process count for no benefit.
raw_findings.impact: N identical cluster-wide memory INFO scans per submit (N = number of flusher processes), each buffer also holding its own duplicate parent-side Redis connection; used and available are each summed N times, adding redundant Redis load with no additional information.
raw_findings.root_cause: The refactor replaced the single shared buffer with per-process buffers and naively fanned out cluster-level memory checks over all of them, though they all target the same cluster.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Query memory info once (e.g. keep a single parent-side SpansBuffer/client for record_stored_segments and get_memory_info) instead of iterating all per-process buffers.
raw_findings.title: Redis cluster memory usage is queried once per flusher buffer against the same cluster
raw_findings.trigger: submit() runs with spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage < 1.0 and multiple flusher processes; every SpansBuffer's get_memory_info() calls iter_cluster_memory_usage on the same SENTRY_SPAN_BUFFER_CLUSTER client.

validated_findings.trigger: Reading the SpanFlusher docstring while the constructor actually creates min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards)) processes, and the consumer CLI passes --flusher-processes with a default of 1, so the common deployment gets a single process handling all shards.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is categorized as 'doc_defect' which is a stylistic/documentation issue. The docstring inaccuracy doesn't cause runtime failures or incorrect behavior - it's misleading documentation, not a functional defect.

validated_findings.body: N identical cluster-wide memory INFO scans per submit (N = number of flusher processes), each buffer also holding its own duplicate parent-side Redis connection; used and available are each summed N times, adding redundant Redis load with no additional information.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Redundant Redis INFO traffic and duplicate connections scale with flusher process count for no benefit.
validated_findings.impact: N identical cluster-wide memory INFO scans per submit (N = number of flusher processes), each buffer also holding its own duplicate parent-side Redis connection; used and available are each summed N times, adding redundant Redis load with no additional information.
validated_findings.root_cause: The refactor replaced the single shared buffer with per-process buffers and naively fanned out cluster-level memory checks over all of them, though they all target the same cluster.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Query memory info once (e.g. keep a single parent-side SpansBuffer/client for record_stored_segments and get_memory_info) instead of iterating all per-process buffers.
validated_findings.title: Redis cluster memory usage is queried once per flusher buffer against the same cluster
validated_findings.trigger: submit() runs with spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage < 1.0 and multiple flusher processes; every SpansBuffer's get_memory_info() calls iter_cluster_memory_usage on the same SENTRY_SPAN_BUFFER_CLUSTER client.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about redundant Redis queries is speculative. Each buffer in self.buffers corresponds to different shards, and get_memory_info() returns cluster-wide memory info. While there may be redundancy, the impact claim of 'N identical cluster-wide memory INFO scans' is not proven from the patch - the buffers may share the same client but the actual Redis call behavior isn't shown to be duplicated N times.
